messages.content: We are ready to start planning a Maine coast trip for September. It will be the two of us from Denver, six nights total, split between Portland and Bar Harbor. I am not sure which city should come first or whether Bangor helps.
What dates are you considering, and do you want exactly two full days available for Acadia rather than counting an arrival or departure day? Also, will you share one hotel room throughout?
September 12 through September 18, 2026. Yes, one room for both of us. I want at least two days when we can wake up near Acadia, spend the entire day there, and return to the same hotel.

That requires at least three nights in Bar Harbor. A three-night Portland and three-night Bar Harbor split works if the transfer day falls between them. The cleanest geographic order is Denver to Portland, three nights there, drive to Bar Harbor on Tuesday, spend Wednesday and Thursday at Acadia, and fly home from Bangor on Friday. Bangor is about 1 hour 15 minutes from Bar Harbor, while returning to Portland takes roughly 3 hours to 3 hours 20 minutes before traffic or stops.
Give me a few complete sequences, not just the airport comparison. I want to see where each night goes and what the travel days would look like.

Sequence A is Portland first with an open-jaw flight: fly Denver to Portland on Saturday, September 12; stay in Portland Saturday through Monday nights; drive to Bar Harbor Tuesday; stay there Tuesday through Thursday nights; use Wednesday and Thursday as full Acadia days; drive to Bangor Friday and fly home. This gives the easiest final ground transfer.

Sequence B reverses it: fly Denver to Bangor Saturday, drive to Bar Harbor, stay Saturday through Monday nights, drive to Portland Tuesday, stay Tuesday through Thursday nights, and fly Portland to Denver Friday. It also protects two full Acadia days, but reaching Bangor from Denver generally requires a connection and could make the first day long.

Sequence C is round trip through Portland: stay in Portland Saturday and Sunday nights, then Bar Harbor Monday through Thursday nights, and return to Portland for the Friday flight. It supplies three full days near Acadia, but Friday requires a long drive before flying. A safer version would move back toward Portland Thursday evening, which undercuts the final Bar Harbor night.
Sequence A sounds best. Is there any meaningful airfare reason to reverse it and start at Bangor?

The likely advantage of starting at Bangor would be a lower fare on a particular connecting itinerary, not better logistics. Portland has more service and may have a Denver nonstop in the September schedule, while Bangor generally means one stop. Starting in Bangor also leaves an hour-plus drive after the flight, when delays and an earlier sunset could make the arrival less pleasant. I would reverse the trip only if the Bangor outbound were substantially less expensive or Bar Harbor lodging were available only for the first three nights.
Then keep Portland first unless the hotel situation forces us to reverse it. What flight pattern are you seeing for that order?

For planning purposes, the strongest pattern is a Saturday morning Denver departure reaching Portland in midafternoon, followed by a Friday Bangor departure around midday with one connection and an early-evening Denver arrival. United is currently displaying a Denver-Portland nonstop on some September dates, while Bangor-Denver options connect through hubs such as Chicago or Newark. Schedules this far out can change, so I would treat the times as provisional until the flights are selected from a live search.

That is fine. Now compare lodging. We do not need luxury, but in Portland I would like to be able to walk to dinner. In Bar Harbor, being in town would be useful unless parking at the hotel becomes a problem.

For Portland, three practical candidates are Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port, Portland Regency Hotel & Spa, and the Courtyard Portland Downtown/Waterfront. All place you within an easy walk of Old Port restaurants. The Hyatt Place is often the simplest functional choice; the Regency has more local character; the Courtyard is closer to the waterfront edge and typically has consistent modern rooms.

For Bar Harbor, I would compare Bar Harbor Grand Hotel, Acadia Hotel-Downtown, and Atlantic Oceanside Hotel. The first two are in or very near the compact town center. Atlantic Oceanside has more on-site space and parking but sits farther from the center, so some evenings may involve a short drive or longer walk.
Can you narrow that to two combinations and account for parking and the fact that Bar Harbor availability may disappear first?

Combination 1 is Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port for September 12-15 and Bar Harbor Grand Hotel for September 15-18. It keeps both stays straightforward, puts the Bar Harbor portion close to restaurants, and commonly includes on-site parking there. Portland parking would normally carry a nightly charge.

Combination 2 is Portland Regency for September 12-15 and Atlantic Oceanside for September 15-18. This trades a more distinctive Portland stay for a Bar Harbor property with easier vehicle handling and more grounds, though it is less convenient for walking into the center.

I would check and hold a refundable Bar Harbor room before settling the Portland property because the three-night Bar Harbor block is the less flexible piece.
Suppose the Bar Harbor Grand only has September 12 through 15. Would reversing the whole trip still preserve what we need?

Yes. You would fly Denver to Bangor on Saturday, September 12, drive to Bar Harbor, and stay through Tuesday morning. Sunday and Monday would be the two full Acadia days. On Tuesday, drive about 3 hours 15 minutes to Portland, stay there Tuesday through Thursday nights, and fly Portland to Denver Friday. The tradeoff is that any delay reaching Bangor on Saturday affects the drive and first hotel arrival, but it does not consume either full park day.
Would you choose that over a different Bar Harbor hotel for September 15 through 18?

No, not solely to obtain the Bar Harbor Grand. Keeping Portland first produces the easier air and driving sequence. I would first look for another acceptable Bar Harbor property for September 15-18. Reversing becomes worthwhile if the remaining later properties are poorly located, unusually expensive, or nonrefundable while the earlier Grand Hotel stay has reasonable terms.
Agreed. Keep the three and three split. I do not want to add an airport hotel or turn the final night into a positioning night.

Then the open-jaw route is the best fit: Portland for the first three nights, Bar Harbor for the final three, and Bangor for the flight home. It preserves both full Acadia days and avoids backtracking to Portland or changing hotels for one night.
Lay out the exact working itinerary with realistic drive windows. Include one primary hotel pair and one fallback pair.

Saturday, September 12: fly Denver to Portland, ideally arriving by midafternoon; collect the rental car and allow about 20 minutes to reach central Portland, plus rental and traffic time. Check in at Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port.

Sunday and Monday: Portland, with both nights at the Hyatt Place.

Tuesday, September 15: check out after breakfast. Leave Portland around 9:30 a.m. The direct drive to Bar Harbor is approximately 3 hours 10 minutes, but allow 4 to 4.5 hours with a meal, fuel, and seasonal traffic. A 1:30 to 2:00 p.m. arrival is realistic. Check in at Bar Harbor Grand Hotel.

Wednesday and Thursday: full Acadia days, returning to Bar Harbor each night.

Friday, September 18: check out and leave Bar Harbor about 2 hours 45 minutes before a Bangor flight's boarding time. The drive is normally 1 hour 15 minutes, and the added margin covers fuel, rental return, and airport processing.

Primary hotels: Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port, September 12-15; Bar Harbor Grand Hotel, September 15-18.

Fallback hotels: Courtyard Portland Downtown/Waterfront, September 12-15; Atlantic Oceanside Hotel, September 15-18.
One correction: do not build Friday around an early flight. After two park days, I would rather have a normal morning and leave Bar Harbor without rushing. What does that do to the flight options?

It points to a Bangor departure no earlier than about noon, with 1:00 to 2:00 p.m. preferable. Leaving Bar Harbor around 9:30 or 10:00 a.m. would provide a normal breakfast and adequate time for the drive, refueling, and rental return. A later Bangor itinerary may reach Denver in the evening and could have a longer connection, but it better matches the final day than choosing the earliest fare.
Good. Give me the final comparison between using Bangor on Friday and simply driving back to Portland for the flight.

Bangor on Friday is the stronger choice. It limits the drive to about 1 hour 15 minutes and allows a relaxed morning, although the flight will probably require one connection and may cost more. Portland could offer a nonstop or broader schedule, but reaching that airport requires roughly 3 hours 15 minutes of driving before allowing for stops, rental return, and airport time. For a comfortable Portland departure, you would need either a late-afternoon flight or a much earlier start from Bar Harbor.

The working plan is therefore Denver to Portland on September 12, three nights in Portland, transfer to Bar Harbor on September 15, three nights there, and Bangor to Denver on September 18 with a departure after noon. The primary hotel pair is Hyatt Place Portland-Old Port and Bar Harbor Grand Hotel; the fallback is Courtyard Portland Downtown/Waterfront and Atlantic Oceanside. Nothing should be booked until the September 15-18 Bar Harbor availability, total hotel prices, cancellation terms, and the live open-jaw flight schedule are checked together.
